title: Tap-to-block ad-hoc unavailability on the schedule calendar (weeks/days/hours)
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- no backend change, the full CRUD API this needs already exists from task 008
keyConstraints: No backend work: GET/POST /admin/availability-exceptions and DELETE /admin/availability-exceptions/:id already exist (backend/src/routes/adminAvailability.ts), already behind requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit, and already validated (backend/src/validation/adminAvailabilitySchema.ts: date as YYYY-MM-DD, type 'blocked'|'open', start_time/end_time as strict HH:MM:SS with end_time after sta_time). Confirmed via backend/src/services/availabilityService.ts's computeAvailableSlots that 'blocked' exceptions are subtracted from whatever the standard weekly rules produce for that date, and subtractIntervals clips a removal interval to the base interval's actual bounds -- so a blocked exception with start_time 00:00:00/end_time 23:59:59 safely blocks a full day regardless of that day's actual configured hours, with no need to know or match the exact rule times. 'Block a week' has no dedicated backend concept -- it is a client-side loop creating one blocked exception row (00:00:00-23:59:59) per date in that week; there is no single-request 'block week' endpoint, so the UI must issue one POST per date and handle partial failure sensibly (e.g. report which dates succeeded/failed rather than silently losing failures). Build this as a new mode on the EXISTING frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx (task 018) rather than a second, separate calendar -- that component already has correct month/week/day navigation, DST-safe positioning via luxon, and a mobile-first layout; duplicating that grid logic in a new screen would re-introduce exactly the kind of date-math risk this project has already paid down. Reuse react-big-calendar's built-in 'selectable' prop and onSelectSlot callback (gives {start, end, action}) for tap/drag-to-select a range in day/week view; for month view, a single tap on a date cell should be treated as 'block that whole day'. Existing bookings and their onSelectEvent/detail-popup behavior (task 018) must be completely unaffected in the default (view) mode -- this is additive only, gated behind an explicit mode toggle (e.g. 'View' vs 'Manage availability').
description: Extend the existing masseur schedule calendar (AdminCalendar.tsx, task 018) with a second mode for managing ad-hoc unavailability, in addition to its current view-only booking display. In 'Manage availability' mode: (1) existing blocked exceptions render on the calendar as a visually distinct background/overlay (e.g. via react-big-calendar's backgroundEvents, styled differently from pending/confirmed bookings); (2) tapping/dragging an empty range in day or week view creates a blocked exception covering that exact time range; (3) tapping a date cell in month view creates a blocked exception covering that entire day; (4) tapping an existing blocked exception offers to remove it (unblock). All mutations go through the existing availability-exceptions API (POST to create, DELETE to remove) -- no new backend surface. Booking display and interaction in the default 'View' mode must remain byte-for-byte the same as task 018 delivered it.
acceptanceCriteria: AdminCalendar gains a View/Manage-availability mode toggle; default mode is unchanged from task 018 (bookings visible, tap-for-detail, no blocking UI)

In Manage-availability mode, existing blocked availability_exceptions (fetched via GET /admin/availability-exceptions) render as a visually distinct overlay, clearly different from pending/confirmed booking events
Day/week view: dragging or tapping-and-selecting an empty time range creates a blocked exception for exactly that range via POST /admin/availability-exceptions
Month view: tapping a date cell creates a full-day blocked exception (00:00:00-23:59:59) for that date via POST /admin/availability-exceptions

Blocking a week is supported by selecting a week's worth of days (e.g. drag across 7 day cells in month view, or an explicit 'block this week' action while in week view) and issues one POST per date; if any individual date fails, the masseur is told which date(s) failed rather than the failure being silent
Tapping an existing blocked exception in Manage-availability mode offers to unblock it (DELETE /admin/availability-exceptions/:id), removing it from the calendar on success
Booking rendering, selection, and detail popup in View mode are unchanged from task 018 -- existing AdminCalendar tests for that behavior still pass unmodified
Layout and tap targets verified usable at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, consistent with task 018's mobile-first requirement
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: backend/src/routes/adminAvailability.ts (existing API, read-only reference -- no changes expected)
backend/src/services/availabilityService.ts (read-only reference -- confirms full-day block semantics via subtractIntervals clipping)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx (extend with the new mode, reusing existing localizer/events setup)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.css (extend with styling for blocked-exception overlay + mode toggle)
frontend/test/AdminCalendar.test.tsx (extend -- existing View-mode assertions must still pass)
frontend/src/api/client.ts and frontend/src/api/types.ts (add availability-exceptions CRUD calls + types)
securityConsiderations: None beyond what already governs the availability-exceptions routes (requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit, unchanged). No new mutation surface at the API level. One practical risk worth the Implementer's attention: a masseur rapidly issuing many POSTs while dragging across a multi-week 'block' selection could be rate-limited by adminRateLimit -- acceptance criteria's partial-failure handling should surface a 429 the same way as any other failed date, not crash the flow.
